title: Finite-quotient cochains compare to all-continuous scalar cochains for pro-prime-to-ell groups
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm topology, and a finite intermediate field $E$. For $F=E$ or $\Omega$ let $A_F(S)=C(S,F)$ with all continuous maps [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], on the small coherent profinite site of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $K$ be a profinite group such that every finite continuous quotient has order prime to $\ell$. Give $F$ the trivial $K$-action. Define a nonnegative complex $\mathcal C_F^\bullet(K)$ of internal $A_F$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] by
$$\mathcal C_F^n(K)(S)=C(S\times K^n,F).$$
Its differential is the trivial-action inhomogeneous differential
$$(dc)(s;g_1,\ldots,g_{n+1})=c(s;g_2,\ldots,g_{n+1})+\sum_{i=1}^{n}(-1)^i c(s;g_1,\ldots,g_i g_{i+1},\ldots,g_{n+1})+(-1)^{n+1}c(s;g_1,\ldots,g_n),$$
with the evident $n=0$ convention $d=0$. Let $\mathcal L_F^n(K)$ be the sheafification of the subpresheaf of these functions which factor, in the group coordinates, through $(K/U)^n$ for some open normal subgroup $U$ of $K$. The coefficient dependence on $S$ is unrestricted and continuous. The differential preserves these subpresheaves, so inclusion gives a canonical cochain map $\iota:\mathcal L_F^\bullet(K)\to\mathcal C_F^\bullet(K)$. This specified map is an isomorphism after localization in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{A_F})$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], that is, a quasi-isomorphism of complexes of sheaves. This compares two explicit continuous-function complexes, without identifying either with derived invariants. The norm topology on the noncomplete $\Omega$ is used throughout.

proof.text: The differential is a finite alternating sum of pullbacks by continuous maps, so it is continuous and $A_F(S)$-linear. The coface relations $\delta_j\delta_i=\delta_i\delta_{j-1}$ for $i<j$ follow from associativity in $K$ (and deleting an endpoint); pairing these equal terms with opposite signs gives $d^2=0$. A function factoring through $(K/U)^n$ retains that property after each face. Intersecting finitely many open normal subgroups provides a common quotient for any finite list of representatives. Thus both complexes and the specified inclusion are defined, and in degree zero they both equal $A_F$ with zero outgoing differential.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent analytic expansion: well-defined differential, finite-quotient subcomplex and degree zero

proof.text:
Let $L_0^\bullet$ denote the finite-quotient subpresheaf before sheafification. Fix $S$ and $n\geq1$. A cocycle $c\in L_0^n(S)$ factors through $Q=K/U$. Its cocycle equation holds on $Q^{n+1}$ since $K\to Q$ is surjective. Put $m=|Q|$ and
$$b(s;g_1,\ldots,g_{n-1})=(-1)^n m^{-1}\sum_{h\in Q}c(s;g_1,\ldots,g_{n-1},h).$$
This is a continuous finite-quotient cochain. Sum the cocycle equation $(dc)(s;g_1,\ldots,g_n,h)=0$ over $h\in Q$. In the last multiplication term replace $g_nh$ by $h$; the first $n$ terms give $d$ of the unsigned sum, and the endpoint term gives $(-1)^{n+1}m c$. Hence $db=c$. For $n=1$ this equality reads $0=c$, consistent with $d^0=0$. It follows that $H^n(L_0^\bullet(S))=0$ for $n>0$, for both coefficient fields; in degree zero it is $C(S,F)$. Only finite sums and $m^{-1}\in F$ occur.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent analytic expansion: finite quotient averaging with the sign and degree-one case

proof.text: For finite $F=E$, completeness and the nonarchimedean inequality are supplied by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-complete] and [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value]. Apply [lem-sfb-prime-to-ell-complete-scalar-integral] and put $h_E c=(-1)^n I_K(c(-,h))$ for a degree-$n$ cocycle. Integrating its cocycle equation gives $d h_E c=c$: left translation by $g_n$ handles the penultimate term, and normalization handles the last term, with the sign computed in step 2. The integral's parameter clause proves continuity, and its bound gives $\|h_E c\|_\infty\leq\|c\|_\infty$. This works for every finite intermediate field, not just the originally fixed $E$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent analytic expansion: bounded finite-field primitives with arbitrary profinite parameters

proof.text: Now let $z\in C(S\times K^n,\Omega)$ be a cocycle, $n\geq1$. Apply [lem-sfb-profinite-metric-function-quotients] to its metric-valued function, obtaining $p:S\twoheadrightarrow S_0$, $q:K\twoheadrightarrow G$ and $z_0\in C(S_0\times G^n,\Omega)$. Surjectivity of $p\times q^{n+1}$ shows $dz_0=0$. Every finite quotient of $G$ is a finite quotient of $K$, so has order prime to $\ell$. It suffices to construct a primitive for $z_0$ and pull it back. Hence, for the next steps, write $S,G,z$ for the metrizable quotients and descended cocycle. If $S$ is empty take the unique zero cochain.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent analytic expansion: reduce a single family to metrizable profinite quotients

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-algcl-countable-closed-finite-cover], choose increasing finite fields $F_i\subseteq\Omega$ covering $\Omega$. For each $i$ choose $p_i:\Omega\to F_i$ by [lem-sfb-norm-one-finite-subfield-projection]. Put $p_{-1}=0$ and $e_i=(p_i-p_{i-1})z$ for $i\geq0$. Each $e_i$ is a continuous $F_i$-valued cocycle, since the projections are $\mathbf Q_\ell$-linear. For each fixed input, $e_i$ is eventually zero: both projections eventually fix its algebraic value. Also $p_i z\to z$ uniformly. Indeed a finite $\epsilon$-net for the compact image of $z$ lies in one $F_N$; for $i\geq N$ the norm-one bound gives $|p_i x-x|\leq\epsilon$ on that image. Consequently $\|e_i\|_\infty\to0$ and $\sum_{i=0}^N e_i=p_Nz$. The projections need not commute with one another.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent analytic expansion: pointwise finite scalar components, uniformly tending to zero

proof.text:
Put $f(s;g_0,\ldots,g_n)=z(s;g_0^{-1}g_1,\ldots,g_{n-1}^{-1}g_n)$. For every $s$, the inverse images of the closed fields $F_N$ cover the nonempty compact Hausdorff space $G^{n+1}$. By [lem-sfb-baire-closed-cover-interior], one has nonempty interior. A product neighbourhood therein contains a rectangle $Ha_0\times\cdots\times Ha_n$ for an open normal $H$. Metrizability and compactness give a countable clopen basis for $G$ (take finite subcovers at each metric scale); every clopen is a finite union of basis elements. There are therefore only countably many such coset rectangles. Enumerate their pairs with field indices as $(B_j,N_j)_{j\geq1}$. Define
$$A_j=\{s\in S:f(s;B_j)\subseteq F_{N_j}\}.$$
Each $A_j$ is closed, being an intersection of inverse images of $F_{N_j}$ under evaluations, and the Baire argument proves $S=\bigcup_j A_j$. No open neighbourhood of $s$ is claimed to lie in $A_j$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent analytic expansion: closed cover by finite-field rectangle certificates for each parameter

proof.text: Choose finite clopen partitions $\mathcal P_i$ of the metrizable profinite $S$, refining one another and with mesh tending to zero. They exist by taking finite clopen refinements of metric-ball covers. Let $U_{j,i}$ be the union of atoms of $\mathcal P_i$ meeting $A_j$. These clopen sets decrease to $A_j$: a point outside the closed $A_j$ is eventually in an atom disjoint from it. Let $k_i(s)$ be the least $j\leq i$ with $s\in U_{j,i}$, or $1$ if none exists; define $k_0=1$. Each $k_i$ is locally constant with finite range. For each $s$, let $j(s)$ be the least index with $s\in A_j$. All smaller indices are eventually excluded from $U_{j,i}$ and $s$ always belongs to $U_{j(s),i}$; hence $k_i(s)=j(s)$ for all sufficiently large $i$. This is eventual stabilization separately at each parameter, with no uniform index or field asserted.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent analytic expansion: explicit locally constant approximations to the least closed-cover certificate

proof.text:
For each rectangle certificate $j$, apply [lem-sfb-bounded-finite-evaluation-rectangle-replacement] to $G,H_j,n,(a_{j,r})$, giving $T_j,R_j$. The index $[G:H_j]$ is prime to $\ell$ because $H_j$ is normal and $G/H_j$ is a finite quotient. Their choices are independent of coefficients. On each clopen piece on which $k_i=j$ is constant, form $r_i(s)=R_j e_i(s)$ and
$$b_i(s)=T_j e_i(s)+h_{F_i}r_i(s).$$
The residual is an $F_i$-valued cocycle, so step 3 supplies its continuous bounded primitive. The finitely many clopen pieces glue these formulas to a continuous $F_i$-valued cochain on $S\times G^{n-1}$. The replacement identity gives $db_i=e_i$, and all three operators have norm bound one; thus $\|b_i\|_\infty\leq\|e_i\|_\infty\to0$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent analytic expansion: finite-field component primitives with a stabilized rectangle correction

proof.text:
Fix $(s,x)\in S\times G^{n-1}$. Eventually $k_i(s)=j=j(s)$ and $i>N_j$. On $B_j$ one has $f(s,-)\in F_{N_j}$; therefore the homogeneous function of $e_i(s,-)$ vanishes there, since both $p_i,p_{i-1}$ fix that field. The rectangle clause of [lem-sfb-bounded-finite-evaluation-rectangle-replacement] gives $R_j e_i(s)=0$ as a whole cochain. Thus eventually
$$b_i(s,x)=(T_j e_i(s))(x)=\sum_{a=1}^{u_j}\alpha_{j,a}e_i(s,\psi_{j,a}(x)).$$
There are only finitely many evaluations in this formula. At each of their fixed inputs, $e_i$ is eventually zero by step 5. Hence $b_i(s,x)=0$ for all sufficiently large $i$. This proves pointwise finiteness of the primitive series, including the parameter points outside every finite initial union of certificates.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent analytic expansion: the missing parametrized selection argument: finite evaluations force pointwise finite primitives

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-normed-field-completion] to view $\Omega$ isometrically in its complete normed field $B$. Its nonarchimedean inequality follows by taking limits of the inequality on finite subextensions. Since $\|b_i\|_\infty\to0$, the ultrametric inequality makes the partial sums uniformly Cauchy on the compact domain: every tail has norm at most $\sup_{i>N}\|b_i\|_\infty$. Completeness gives a uniform limit $b:S\times G^{n-1}\to B$. To check continuity directly, fix a point and $\epsilon>0$, choose a uniformly $\epsilon$-close continuous partial sum, and use continuity of that sum and the ultrametric triangle inequality. Step 9 says each value of $b$ is actually a finite sum in $\Omega$. The subspace metric on $\Omega\subseteq B$ then makes $b$ norm-continuous into $\Omega$. Since $d$ is a finite sum of evaluations, $db=\lim_N d(\sum_{i\leq N}b_i)=\lim_N p_Nz=z$. Pullback as in step 4 proves objectwise positive-degree exactness for every original profinite $S$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent analytic expansion: uniform convergence in the completion, with algebraic values by pointwise finiteness

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact] with the constant ring $R=\mathbf Z$, to the underlying abelian presheaf complexes. By step 2 the sheafification of $L_0^\bullet$ has cohomology $A_F$ in degree zero and zero in positive degrees. The continuous-function complex is already a sheaf complex, and steps 3 and 10 say that every positive-degree kernel section lies in the image locally on a cover; its cohomology sheaves therefore vanish. Both complexes are zero in negative degrees. The inclusion is the identity in degree zero by step 1, so it induces isomorphisms on every underlying abelian cohomology sheaf. Kernels are stable submodules and images are the sheafifications of the stable pointwise images; these carry the inherited $A_F$-actions. Consequently the same inclusion induces isomorphisms on module cohomology and is a quasi-isomorphism of internal $A_F$-module complexes.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent analytic expansion: exact sheafification and the specified inclusion on cohomology

proof.text: By [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], localization at quasi-isomorphisms inverts this specified inclusion, giving the asserted isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{A_F})$. If $S$ is empty all positive-degree section groups are zero. If $K=1$, the alternating differential is zero in even degree and the identity in odd positive degree, giving the same positive-degree acyclicity. Finite $K$ is already covered by the finite formula in step 2. These checks do not require $\Omega$ to be complete.
